record.context_brief: bounded operator representation of overcomplete Gabor frames
record.original_question: Do there exist overcomplete Gabor frames for L^2(R), meaning systems of the form {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} with g in L^2(R) and parameters a,b>0 that form a frame but not a Riesz basis, together with some ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the frame elements, such that the ordered frame can be written as {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded linear operator T and some vector phi?

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Does there exist overcomplete Gabor frames {EmbTnag}m,n∈Z and an appropriate ordering on the form {fk}k∈I , such that the operator T in (2.3) is bounded?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$. For $a,b>0$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the translation operator $T_a g(x)=g(x-a)$ and the modulation operator $E_b g(x)=e^{2\pi i b x}g(x)$. The associated Gabor system is $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$. A countable family $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R})$ is called a frame if there exist constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ such that
$$A\|f\|^2\le\sum_{k\in I}|\langle f,f_k\rangle|^2\le B\|f\|^2,\qquad \forall f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}),$$
and a Riesz basis if it is the image of an orthonormal basis under a bounded invertible operator. The frame is called overcomplete if it is a frame but not a Riesz basis.

Question: Do there exist parameters $a,b>0$ and a window $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that the Gabor system $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, together with a bijection $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ (for some index set $I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$ or $\mathbb{N}$) ordering its elements, a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$, and a vector $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, such that
$$\{f_k\}_{k\in I}=\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: For the index set $I=\mathbb{N}_0$, a complete negative answer has been established: any norm-bounded overcomplete frame, in particular any overcomplete Gabor frame, cannot be represented as the orbit $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\ge 0}$ of a bounded operator. For the two-sided index set $I=\mathbb{Z}$, only partial negative results are known (e.g. for specific classes of overcomplete Gabor frames the representation as an orbit of a bounded invertible operator is impossible), and the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Orbits of bounded bijective operators and Gabor frames
status_evidence.snippet: Two classes of overcomplete Gabor frames which cannot be ordered over Z and represented by orbits of operators in GL(L^2(R)) are given.
status_evidence.claim: Partial negative results for the Z-indexed case.

status_evidence.title: Frame Properties of Operator Orbits
status_evidence.snippet: An overcomplete Gabor or wavelet frame can never be written in the form (T^n f_0)_{n in N} with a bounded operator T.
status_evidence.claim: Negative answer for one-sided orbits N_0.

status_evidence.title: Frames, operator representations, and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: For frames of this type the existence of such a representation has only been confirmed in the case of Riesz bases.
status_evidence.claim: The general Z-indexed problem is still considered open.
